evidence.description: Login registers a visit and logout resets seed state, but neither branch updates the published authentication or profile properties.
Authentication state is refreshed in the separate profile-update handler, with isLoggedIn additionally deferred into an unstructured task.
The published isLoggedIn value determines whether refreshing state fetches server data or collects guest seeds.

candidates.explanation: The authentication-state notification handler performs login/logout side effects without updating isLoggedIn or the published profile fields. Those fields are refreshed only by a separate profile-update notification. Consequently, an authentication-state notification alone leaves the provider exposing its previous authentication state, and refreshSeedState can select the wrong logged-in or guest path. The profile-update handler also defers isLoggedIn into another task while updating the profile fields immediately.
candidates.title: Authentication changes do not synchronize published authentication state

evidence.description: The task captures an access token, awaits the request, then unconditionally updates balance or error state without cancellation or a session-validity check.
Applying a response changes the published level, progress, and seed balance.
Logout resets local balance and level, but does not invalidate outstanding visit requests.

candidates.explanation: Each visit registration launches an untracked task and applies its response after the network suspension without checking whether the authentication session is still current. A request started before logout can therefore overwrite the local seed and level reset with authenticated account data. Repeated refreshes can also create overlapping requests whose responses are applied in completion order rather than request order.
candidates.title: In-flight visit requests can apply results after authentication changes

evidence.description: Each animation assigns its captured balance after a delay and independently clears the shared increment indicator after another delay.
A newer response can assign seedCount immediately even while an earlier animated assignment remains queued.
The logout reset updates seedCount without invalidating previously scheduled animation closures.

candidates.explanation: Balance updates are deferred through uncancellable delayed closures, with no check that the scheduled value is still current. A pending animation can overwrite a subsequent balance update or logout reset. Overlapping animations also schedule independent clearing operations, allowing an older animation to clear the increment indicator belonging to a newer one.
candidates.title: Delayed balance animations can overwrite newer state
